moduleTitle: Integrating Tricentis Testim with Continuous Integration (CI) Tools
learningObjectives: Explain how the Testim CLI enables integration with virtually any CI tool.
Identify which major CI/VCS platforms Testim integrates with out of the box.

elements.term: The CLI as the integration point
elements.description: CI can invoke the npm-based Testim CLI when its runner has a supported Node.js environment, configured credentials/project/grid and required network access. Shell capability alone does not guarantee a working integration.

The CI documentation links platform-specific runner guides such as Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, GitLab and others. A guide listing does not establish universal out-of-box branch mirroring or automatic pipeline provisioning.

elements.title: Full list of named CI/VCS integrations (Tricentis docs)

bulletPoints: Invoke the CLI from a suitably configured CI runner; inspect dependencies, credentials, connectivity and results.
Named integrations include Jenkins (standard + Docker), Azure Pipelines, Bamboo, CircleCI, Codeship, TeamCity, Visual Studio, and GitLab.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Setting up and monitoring a CI integration

elements.description: Settings > CLI > CI provides a platform-specific starting command. Adapt it to the runner and actual selection/configuration; configure safe credential handling and a JUnit report path that the CI collector also reads.

Inspect the applicable test/execution result and time-filtered history. Correlate them with the actual CI build; a chart or copied command does not by itself prove the pipeline completed or identify every failure cause.

bulletPoints: Generate the starting command, then configure runner, credentials and report collection.
Monitoring: one click opens the relevant test result for a build; historical analytics are filterable by time period.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming CI integration requires a unique plugin per tool
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing each CI system needs its own bespoke Testim plugin before tests can be triggered from it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Basic CLI invocation does not require a bespoke plugin, but the runner still needs supported dependencies, credentials and connectivity. Platform guides do not automatically configure a pipeline.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What enables basic CI invocation of Testim, once the runner’s dependencies, credentials and connectivity are configured?

options.text: It requires a unique, custom-built plugin for every CI platform.
It runs as a simple shell command, which any CI tool capable of running shell commands can invoke.
It only works with Jenkins.
CI integration is not supported by Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the lowest common denominator every CI tool supports.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The CLI is an invocable command in a supported configured runner. A platform-specific plugin is not inherently required for basic invocation; shell capability alone does not guarantee successful execution.

optionExplanations.A: A bespoke plugin is not inherently required for basic CLI invocation.
optionExplanations.B: The configured CLI runner can invoke the command.
optionExplanations.C: The documented integration is not Jenkins-only.
optionExplanations.D: Basic CLI-based CI integration is documented.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of these is a named CI/VCS platform Testim integrates with?

options.text: Jenkins
Microsoft Paint
Adobe Photoshop
None — Testim has no CI integrations

practiceQuiz.rationale: Jenkins has a documented CI integration guide. This establishes documented runner setup, not automatic provisioning of every CI feature.

optionExplanations.A: Jenkins has a documented CI guide.
optionExplanations.B: Paint is not in that platform-specific CI list.
optionExplanations.C: Photoshop is not in that CI list.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation provides multiple CI guides.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of these is absent from the listed platform-specific CI guides on the cited CI integrations page?

options.text: Bamboo
TeamCity
CircleCI
Basecamp

practiceQuiz.hint: One of these is a project-management tool, not a CI/VCS platform.
practiceQuiz.rationale: That page lists Bamboo, TeamCity and CircleCI guides; Basecamp is absent from that specific list. Absence from a list is not proof every possible custom integration is prohibited.

optionExplanations.A: Bamboo is in the cited list.
optionExplanations.B: TeamCity is in the cited list.
optionExplanations.C: CircleCI is in the cited list.
optionExplanations.D: Basecamp is absent from that page’s listed guides.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which settings path provides a platform-specific starting CI command to adapt to your runner?

options.text: Settings > CLI > CI, then select your CI platform from a dropdown and copy the generated command.
Integrations > Test Management > CI.
Reports > Export > CI Command.
There is no dedicated settings page — commands must be typed manually.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same CLI settings page covered elsewhere in this path.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Settings > CLI > CI provides the starting command. Runner setup, credentials, selection and report collection must still be configured and validated.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented starting-command path.
optionExplanations.B: This is not the cited CLI command-generation path.
optionExplanations.C: Report export is not CI command generation.
optionExplanations.D: The dedicated CLI settings workflow exists.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Once a CI integration is running, what can you do from Testim to diagnose a build failure?

options.text: Nothing — CI results aren't visible inside Testim at all.
Inspect the applicable test/execution result and time-filtered history, correlated with the CI build.
Only see a raw pass/fail count with no drill-down.
Automatically fix the failing test without any review.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a direct link from a build to its underlying test result.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Result details and historical analytics support investigation. Correlate them with CI evidence; they do not automatically remediate a failed build.

optionExplanations.A: Applicable run results can be inspected in Testim.
optionExplanations.B: Run details and history help investigation when correlated with CI evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Details go beyond a raw count.
optionExplanations.D: Results do not automatically fix failures.

quickRecap.value: Invoke from a supported configured CI runner; dependencies, credentials and network access still matter.
Jenkins (+ Docker), Azure Pipelines, Bamboo, CircleCI, Codeship, TeamCity, Visual Studio, GitLab.
Settings > CLI > CI provides a starting command; configure and validate the runner/report path.
Inspect run details/history and correlate with actual CI build evidence.
